document.description: Identifier of the Elementor document to change. Call elementor-document-list for the documents Elementor controls.

elementId.description: Stable identifier of the element to act on, exactly as elementor-document-get reports it.

type.description: The WordPress post type: page, post, or elementor_library for a saved template.

status.description: The WordPress post status, such as publish or draft.

editMode.description: The stored Elementor edit mode, normally builder. Empty when the stored value is unreadable.

id.description: The element's stored identifier, exactly as requested.

elType.description: The element type Elementor stores, such as widget or container.

widgetType.description: The widget type when this element renders a widget, null otherwise.

kind.description: Whether this element is a widget or a structural container. An element of unknown type is reported as a container.

label.description: DERIVED, for display only. Computed from the element type on every read; no stored row holds it and it must never be treated as stored state.

path.description: DERIVED position as parentId/index, for display only. It is not an address: any insertion or removal before this element changes it. Address elements by id.

childCount.description: How many elements this one directly contains. Read the subtree with elementor-document-get.

storedSettings.description: The element's settings exactly as the document stores them. A key the element does not store is ABSENT rather than null: the element uses its control default, which elementor-control-schema reports. No default is merged in here.
